data.angle: Explain how to vet an AI SEO agency through repeatable measurement, third-party citation opportunities, clear delivery responsibilities, and written commercial terms, while treating Searchbloom’s self-ranking as a publisher claim rather than an independent verdict.

ranked_sections.reason: Selected as the buyer-focused backbone: connects business outcomes to dated evidence, tracking methods, technical implementation, outside-page opportunities, and written fees and terms.
Selected to explain repeatable measurement across platforms and prompt types, distinguishing visibility signals from leads and revenue.
Selected to define the underlying work—technical SEO, content, entity consistency, and third-party mentions—while keeping the citation-source findings attributed to Searchbloom’s own tracking.
Selected to clarify agency versus client responsibilities and identify concrete warning signs, including missing tracking details and citation-only reporting.
Selected for concrete published fees, minimums, and contract terms, with unpublished information explicitly distinguished from confirmed commercial commitments.
Selected to expose the publisher’s five equally weighted scoring criteria and preserve its disclosures that case-study figures are agency-reported and no company paid for placement.
Selected to preserve the author’s disclosure that Searchbloom publishes the list and ranks itself first, alongside concessions that competitors publish more original research or fuller terms.
Excluded because its publication-transparency checklist overlaps the selected pricing and due-diligence sections; a published item also does not independently establish service quality.
Excluded because its broad timing expectations combine different agency-reported outcomes and would distract from evaluating the evidence and scope of a proposed engagement.
Excluded because nine lengthy profiles would turn the explainer into a directory, although their case-study periods and implementation limitations could support a separate agency-comparison story.
Excluded because its headline recommendations and summary statistics duplicate selected material; its publisher and self-ranking disclosures are preserved through the author’s note instead.
Excluded because situation-specific agency picks broaden the story into recommendations rather than explaining how buyers should test agency fit and evidence.
Excluded because the publisher-assigned totals encourage a league-table reading, while the selected methodology and commercial details better support independent buyer scrutiny.
Excluded because the claimed 2026 Google changes introduce a separate platform-policy narrative that is unnecessary to the focused agency-vetting explanation.
Excluded because the FAQ largely repeats measurement, costs, outsourcing, and agency recommendations already covered more directly in the selected sections.
